Declare a data frame as a panel

Source: R/panel.R
as_panel.Rd

Tell panelviz which column(s) identify the individual and which column is time. The time format is detected automatically (Date, POSIXct, years, two-digit years, "1998 Q1", "2020-03", ISO weeks, "3/14/2021", yyyymm, yyyymmdd, Stata %tm/%tq/%ty values, plain integers).

Usage

as_panel(
  data,
  id,
  time,
  time_format = NULL,
  dups = c("error", "keep"),
  source = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format (one row per individual and time).

id

Column(s) identifying the individual (a subject, unit, entity, participant, firm or country in other fields). Several columns are combined into one composite key. Unquoted names or strings.

time

The time column (a wave, occasion, visit, period or year in other fields).

time_format

NULL (auto-detect), a strptime() string, or one of "year", "quarter", "month", "week", "index".

dups

What to do when an individual has several rows at the same time: "error" (default) or "keep".

source

Where the data comes from, e.g. "BLS; company reports". Shown as "Source: ..." in every chart footer.

Value

A tidy_panel: the data plus standardised .id and .time columns, with the panel structure stored in attr(, "panel").

Examples

d <- data.frame(who = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 4),
                when = rep(c("2020 Q1", "2020 Q2", "2020 Q3", "2020 Q4"), 2),
                y = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 2, 3, 5, 8))
as_panel(d, id = who, time = when)
#> # A tidy panel: 2 individuals x 4 periods (quarter), 2020-01-01 to 2020-10-01
#> # id = who | time = when | balanced | 8 obs
#> # A tibble: 8 × 5
#>   .id   .time      who   when        y
#> * <chr> <date>     <chr> <chr>   <dbl>
#> 1 a     2020-01-01 a     2020 Q1     1
#> 2 a     2020-04-01 a     2020 Q2     2
#> 3 a     2020-07-01 a     2020 Q3     3
#> 4 a     2020-10-01 a     2020 Q4     4
#> 5 b     2020-01-01 b     2020 Q1     2
#> 6 b     2020-04-01 b     2020 Q2     3
#> 7 b     2020-07-01 b     2020 Q3     5
#> 8 b     2020-10-01 b     2020 Q4     8
